code='''def transform(grid):
    # Identify hollow rectangular frames by color. Fill the interior of the frame
    # whose color matches the center cell of the separate 3x3 marker.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    from collections import Counter
    counts = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    bg = counts.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Find 3x3 solid-border marker with a distinct center color and background interior.
    marker_center = None
    for r in range(h-2):
        for c in range(w-2):
            border = [grid[r][c+i] for i in range(3)] + [grid[r+2][c+i] for i in range(3)] + [grid[r+1][c],grid[r+1][c+2]]
            center = grid[r+1][c+1]
            if center != bg and all(x != bg for x in border) and len(set(border)) == 1 and border[0] != center:
                marker_center = center
                break
        if marker_center is not None: break
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    if marker_center is None: return out
    # Find rectangular frame made of marker_center, with interior background.
    for r1 in range(h):
        for r2 in range(r1+2,h):
            for c1 in range(w):
                for c2 in range(c1+2,w):
                    if all(grid[r1][c] == marker_center and grid[r2][c] == marker_center for c in range(c1,c2+1)) and all(grid[r][c1] == marker_center and grid[r][c2] == marker_center for r in range(r1,r2+1)):
                        # Make sure there is at least one interior background cell and frame is rectangular.
                        if all(grid[r][c] == bg for r in range(r1+1,r2) for c in range(c1+1,c2)):
                            fill = next((v for v in counts if v not in (bg, marker_center)), bg)
                            for r in range(r1+1,r2):
                                for c in range(c1+1,c2): out[r][c] = fill
                            return out
    return out
'''

code='''def transform(grid):
    """Fill the interiors of rectangular outlines using their paired color.

    Each outline's color is paired with its adjacent palette color: even n -> n+1,
    odd n -> n-1. The background and outline are preserved.

    from collections import Counter
    bg = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    # Find monochrome rectangular borders enclosing only background cells.
    for color in set(v for row in grid for v in row if v != bg):
        for r1 in range(h):
            for r2 in range(r1 + 2, h):
                for c1 in range(w):
                    for c2 in range(c1 + 2, w):
                        if not (all(grid[r1][c] == color and grid[r2][c] == color for c in range(c1, c2 + 1)) and
                                all(grid[r][c1] == color and grid[r][c2] == color for r in range(r1, r2 + 1))):
                            continue
                        if all(grid[r][c] == bg for r in range(r1 + 1, r2) for c in range(c1 + 1, c2)):
                            fill = color + 1 if color % 2 == 0 else color - 1
                            for r in range(r1 + 1, r2):
                                for c in range(c1 + 1, c2):
                                    out[r][c] = fill
    return out
'''
